prompt: Complete the immutable ImmutableAccount class: withDeposit(amount) and withOwner(name) must each return a NEW account reflecting the change while the original object stays exactly as it was.
explanation: Final fields make the object's state permanent, so the with- methods express change by constructing a new object that copies the untouched field and replaces the changed one -- the same style java.time uses (plusDays, withYear). Callers holding a reference to the original are unaffected, which makes immutable objects safe to share freely across the program. Chaining works because each call returns a fresh, fully-formed instance.
hints: You cannot assign to a final field after construction -- so build a new ImmutableAccount instead.
withDeposit passes the SAME owner and balance + amount to the constructor.
withOwner passes the new owner and the SAME balance; neither method touches this object's fields.
